title: A repo has one project: the server refuses a second

story.i_want_to: have loopctl refuse a second project for a repo that already has one, and name the existing one
story.so_that: every tool and every session on that repo uses one project and one channel

rationale: Mark, 2026-11-19 (docs/factory/architecture.md R5): 'somebody/something continues to create additional channels instead of reusing the same single channel per repo'. Nothing stops it today: Project.create_changeset/2 (lib/loopctl/projects/project.ex:83) checks slug uniqueness only, so four repos carry a kb scope with the repo_url plus a repo_url-less work project that an intake source binds instead, and loopctl#1067 was the cost. The fix is a server-side identity for a repo and a unique index on it, so no client hook is needed.

acceptance_criteria.description: Projects carry a repo_key column: the lowercased host/owner/repo derived from repo_url by the same normalization Projects.resolve_project/2 uses (https and ssh forms, a trailing .git and a trailing slash all give one key); nil when repo_url is nil or blank. It is set in the changeset from repo_url, never cast.

A partial unique index projects_tenant_repo_key_active_uidx on (tenant_id, repo_key) WHERE status = 'active' AND repo_key IS NOT NULL; its migration backfills repo_key for every existing row and fails loudly, naming the colliding project ids, if two active projects of one tenant share a key.

Projects.create_project/3, for kind :work and :kb alike, returns {:error, {:repo_has_project, existing_project_id}} when an active project of the tenant already has the same repo_key; the index's constraint error is mapped to the same tuple, so two concurrent creates yield one project and one refusal.
Projects.update_project/4 and the restore of an archived project return the same refusal when the new or restored repo_key is held by another active project of the tenant.

POST /api/v1/projects, POST /api/v1/kb-scopes, PATCH /api/v1/projects/:id and POST /api/v1/projects/:id/restore answer the refusal with 409, error.code repo_already_has_project, error.existing_project_id, and a message naming the existing project's slug and telling the caller to use it.

Intake.create_source/3 refuses binding repo R to project P when another active project of the tenant has the repo_key of R: {:error, {:repo_has_project, existing_project_id}}, rendered by the intake source controller as the same 409. (update_source/4 cannot change a source's repo or project: @updatable_fields, lib/loopctl/intake.ex:585.)
Another tenant holding a project for the same repo does not block the create: the index and the check are tenant-scoped.

The MCP tools create_project, create_kb_scope, update_project and intake_source_enroll say in their descriptions that a repo already held by a project is refused with 409 repo_already_has_project naming that project's id.

test_cases.name: repo_key normalization
preconditions: Project.repo_key/1 (or the changeset) on several URL spellings
expected_results: the first three give "github.com/mkreyman/chg"; nil gives nil

test_cases.name: a second project on one repo is refused, either kind (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant = fixture(:tenant); fixture(:project, %{tenant_id: tenant.id, kind: :kb, slug: "chg", repo_url: "git@github.com:mkreyman/chg.git"})

test_cases.name: the index decides a race: an insert bypassing the pre-check maps the constraint to the refusal (DataCase)
preconditions: an active project holding the repo_key
steps: insert a second changeset straight through AdminRepo.insert with the same repo_key
expected_results: {:error, {:repo_has_project, first.id}}, not a raised constraint error

test_cases.name: update and restore onto a held repo are refused; an archived holder does not block (DataCase)
preconditions: project A active on repo R; project B active with no repo_url; project C archived on repo R

test_cases.name: 409 body on each project route (ConnCase)
preconditions: a human-anchored tenant with an active project on repo R; a user key and an orchestrator key
steps: PATCH another project to repo R
restore an archived project on R
expected_results: each 409 with code repo_already_has_project and existing_project_id of the holder

test_cases.name: an intake source cannot bind a repo to a project that does not hold it (DataCase + ConnCase)
preconditions: kb scope K holds repo mkreyman/chg; work project W has no repo_url

test_cases.name: tenant isolation: another tenant's project on the repo does not block (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant A holds repo R; tenant B holds none

test_cases.name: tool descriptions name the refusal
steps: read the four tools' descriptions in node --test

technical_notes: Project schema: lib/loopctl/projects/project.ex:59-72; create_changeset/2 at :83, update_changeset at ~:105; slug_unique_constraint/1 at :120 is the pattern for the new unique_constraint.

Normalization exists privately in Projects: normalize_repo_url/1 at lib/loopctl/projects.ex:835 and repo_ref/1 at :852. Move the key derivation into one public function (Projects.repo_key/1 or Project.repo_key/1) and have resolve_by_repo_url/2 (:739) and the changeset both call it, so the index and the resolver can never disagree.

create_project/3 at lib/loopctl/projects.ex:44 (kind set on the struct at :51-54); update_project/4 at :338; restore is ProjectController.restore/2 at lib/loopctl_web/controllers/project_controller.ex:509; create/2 at :268, create_kb_scope/2 at :305, update/2 at :470.

Intake.create_source/3 at lib/loopctl/intake.ex:259 builds the changeset through put_project/3 (:323); add the repo check there, reading the source's repo_full_name against Projects.repo_key/1 of github.com/<repo_full_name>. update_source/4 is at :603.

The 409 is rendered in FallbackController (lib/loopctl_web/fallback_controller.ex) from {:error, {:repo_has_project, id}}, and added to each route's operation/2 responses (CLAUDE.md, Doc hygiene: new API constraint).

Existing production data has no active duplicate repo_url (list_projects, 2026-11-19): the four duplicate pairs hold their repo on the kb scope only, so the backfill and index succeed; 52.3 merges the pairs.

MCP: tool declarations in mcp-server/index.js (create_project at ~:3866, create_kb_scope at ~:3897); the handoff tool (~:3949) resolves before creating a kb scope, so it already reuses the existing project.
Migration: name it after git fetch origin (README Lanes rule 3); the backfill runs in the migration in Elixir with the same repo_key function, and raises with the colliding ids rather than skipping.
non_goals: Merging the existing duplicate pairs: US-52.2 (the operation) and US-52.3 (running it).
Promoting a kb scope to a work project when delivery starts: US-52.3.
Any client-side hook change in claude-config: the server is the only enforcement.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: every check is a read and an insert against loopctl's own database inside one request; no second service holds a project.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.1.2: the repo's owner is decided by projects.repo_key under a unique index, so a restart or deploy loses nothing and no cache can disagree.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.1.3: a retried create meets the index and gets the same refusal naming the same project, so a retry never makes a second project.
failure_modes.slow: n/a: one indexed lookup per create; no network call.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: runs inline in the request process; nothing is queued.

definition_of_done: On production after deploy: SELECT tenant_id, repo_key, count(*) FROM projects WHERE status = 'active' AND repo_key IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING count(*) > 1 returns no rows.
create_kb_scope for git@github.com:mkreyman/chg.git from an MCP session returns 409 repo_already_has_project with existing_project_id eba0b4df-e9ab-4908-a316-f55c698fe8bd.
